classification.difficultyReason: Mentally join P to Q, use reverse bearings to find the included angle and exploit equal sides to obtain a base angle before calculating the requested bearing.

spec.description: Equilateral triangle PCQ with three north arrows, three matching single side ticks and a 20-degree bearing from P to C.
spec.mathematics: PC=CQ=PQ; bearing of C from P is 020 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 20-degree angle is visible; the requested bearing is omitted.

answer.worked:
All three sides are equal, so $\angle CPQ=60^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Bearing of }Q\text{ from }P&=20^\circ+60^\circ\\&=080^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Equal connected legs PC and CQ, with north arrows at P, C and Q. PQ is not drawn.
spec.mathematics: PC=CQ; bearings PC=030 degrees and CQ=060 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Given angles only; no requested bearing or construction PQ.

answer.worked:
The bearing of $P$ from $C$ is $30^\circ+180^\circ=210^\circ$, so the angle between $CP$ and $CQ$ is $210^\circ-60^\circ=150^\circ$.
Since $PC=CQ$, the base angles of triangle $PCQ$ are equal.
$$\begin{align*}\angle CPQ&=\frac{180^\circ-150^\circ}{2}\\&=15^\circ\\\text{Bearing of }Q\text{ from }P&=30^\circ+15^\circ\\&=045^\circ\end{align*}$$

answer.worked:
